cells.tense: Right now the ending has been made and the ground is clear.
cells.act: let the feeling settle into its own depth
cells.ask: Take a quiet half hour with what you feel about what ended. Let it settle at the pace it wants. No prodding, no naming it, no deciding whether you're finished.
cells.core:
You can sit with an ending without hurrying it. Something closed for you — a role, a tie, a version of how things were going to go — and you're not rehearsing it or grieving to a schedule. You met what it asked for and left the ground bare. That's the work, and you're doing it.

The thing worth feeding is quieter than that. Give one half hour to the ending and nothing else — no plan for next, no summary of what it taught you. Whatever comes up is what comes up. You find out what you actually know about it, as opposed to the things you've already settled.
cells.sheetLine: You can let an ending be finished without rushing what comes next.
cells.verb: To let the mind go all the way down into what it knows until it touches its limit.
cells.place: Inside the clearing where something has ended and the ground is bare.

cells.tense: The ending being finished is coming, and the clear ground stays a picture that won't hold still.
cells.act: put the frame on the table before anyone asks
cells.ask: Before anyone asks, say out loud what has actually ended. No softening, no spin, no list of what comes next.
cells.core:
You see what's finished before the people next to you do, and you're already speaking for the gap: calling the ending before it arrives, announcing what stops, giving it a shape out loud. That steadiness holds people up. It also keeps you moving faster than the ground has.

What there is to feed now is quieter. Before anyone asks where things stand, say plainly what is over — no taking it back, no plan stapled to the end of it. Say it the way you'd tell someone which road you're on. The ending gets to be real in the same week you announced it.
cells.sheetLine: You've made the ending a headline. Say it plainly, once.
cells.verb: To let the mind go all the way down into what it knows until it touches its limit.

cells.tense: An ending happened and there you are, still fixed at the closed doorway.
cells.act: mark the good thing together, the day it happens
cells.ask: When something goes well this week, mark it with whoever it belongs to the same day. Not later, not by yourself.
cells.core:
Something ended while your attention kept looking back, and you haven't been at the ending itself lately. You know what moving on looks like when it's going well: you're a person who can stand in an ordinary good evening and be in it — someone's first day, tea being made, a friend finishing a shift — and feel the good of it without reaching back for what closed. People move over ground like that. You've been staying at the threshold.

Go where the day is. Mark one thing going well with whoever else it involves, the day it goes well. Get there from the gladness, not from effort. Three weeks of that is shorter than three weeks at a closed door.

cells.tense: The ending is already finished and done before anyone, including you, has named it as a choice.
cells.act: sit with what the heart already knows
cells.ask: Sit somewhere quiet with whatever you carry about the ending. Don't analyze it, don't fix it, don't act on it — just stay with it a while.
cells.core:
There's a hand in this ending. Not only the one it landed on — the one who had the hard conversation, cleared the space, closed the drawer. Asked about it, you'd say it worked out that way. Life moved. When this part is going well you can look at a thing you did and simply have done it, without the credit and without the argument.

Stay with one part of the ending this week and hold it as yours. Put your own hand on the record, where nobody else can see it. Everything cleared there was cleared by someone. A thing you did can be held without becoming a story you carry.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that a weeks-long arrangement for these four outcomes is the way through this clearing — the record only says writing things down serves the balance, the ask survives that. A reasonable reader could say the leaving was chosen, planned, and is simply practical, not something 'quieter than chosen'. Reading it that way costs them nothing and the act still stands — the asks all work whether the ending was chosen or arrived. The line that serves me is 'the ground is clear and something in you is still standing at the old doorway' — it's a better sentence than the truth of it, which is only that the attention hasn't moved.
